label: LTX Refine
description: LTX-2.5 Tiled Fusion with the Refine Details IC-LoRA: re-renders a frame range with new detail at the output size you pick. Output: an EXR sequence in ACES2065-1 at the upscaled size, plate frame numbers, no audio.
usage: Re-renders a frame range at the output size you pick, generating new detail (LTX-2.5 Tiled Fusion).
Whole input range is sent; tick 'input range' to send only first-last.
prompt is optional: describe only look and style. Don't name objects or people, as they can stamp into every tile.
'tile size' is how much the model sees at once: bigger = more context, more VRAM. If it crashes, lower tile size, output size or the frame count.
Detail is generated, so faces, text and fine patterns can drift. On 'clip', values above 1 are cut and the result stays in 0-1. Check it against the plate.

highlights: 'roll off' (default) compresses values above 1 going in: highlights return approximate, saturated colours shift, deep shadows are crushed and new near-whites come back hot. 'clip' cuts at 1 and keeps shadows open.

License (checked 2026-11): LTX-2.x Community - commercial use is free under $10M annual revenue (affiliates count); above that needs a paid license. Generated content must be disclosed as machine-generated when distributed.

max_frames_input.tooltip: Longer ranges need more VRAM and RAM.

output.tooltip: LTX works on display-referred images, so highlights are rolled off or clipped (see the highlights knob). The result is at the upscaled size, not the plate's.

knobs.name: prompt
knobs.label: prompt
knobs.tooltip: Optional. Look and style only: lighting, palette, film stock, sharpness, grade. The plate supplies the scene. Anything you name can stamp into every tile.

knobs.name: refine_prompt
knobs.label: refine prompt
knobs.tooltip: Let the local Gemma enhancer rewrite the prompt first (from the text only, it doesn't see the plate). Slower, and it can add objects that stamp into the tiles.

knobs.name: output_size
knobs.label: output size
knobs.tooltip: Final canvas long edge: FullHD 1920, 4K 3840, 8K 7680. 8K is untested here and likely to run out of memory.

knobs.name: tile_size
knobs.label: tile size
knobs.tooltip: Long edge of each tile: qHD 960, HD 1280, FullHD 1920. Bigger = more context for the model, more VRAM.

knobs.name: highlights
knobs.label: highlights
knobs.tooltip: roll off (default): the plate and refs go in through ACES Output - sRGB and the result comes back through its inverse, so highlights are compressed instead of cut. Highlights come back approximate, saturated colours shift, deep shadows are crushed, and new near-white pixels come back hot (display 0.98 = about 7, 1.0 = about 16). clip: values above 1 reach the model as 1 (colorimetric), shadows stay open. Comp only the changed area.

knobs.name: lora_strength
knobs.label: LoRA strength
knobs.tooltip: Strength of the Refine Details IC-LoRA.

knobs.name: tiled_encode
knobs.label: use tiled encode
knobs.tooltip: Encode the guide video in tiles to lower the GPU load at big sizes. Off is how Lightricks' workflow ships: less risk of tile effects, but a 4K guide can crash the GPU.
